info.title: watchcat-agent
info.summary: Host metrics endpoint scraped by Prometheus.
info.description:
HTTP surface of `watchcat-agent`, the host metrics agent that runs as a
background service on Linux, Windows and macOS.

The agent is a **pull target**: it never initiates outbound connections. A
remote Prometheus server scrapes `GET /metrics` on an interval and stores
the result. The other two endpoints exist for health checking and for a
human opening the port in a browser.

### Configurable surface

Two things in this document are configuration, not constants:

- **The metrics path.** `/metrics` is the default; `server.metrics_path` in
  the agent config moves it (e.g. `/internal/metrics`). Only that one route
  moves — `/` and `/healthz` are fixed.
- **Scheme and port.** The default listener is `http://0.0.0.0:9800`.
  Setting `server.tls_cert_file` and `server.tls_key_file` switches it to
  HTTPS (TLS 1.2 minimum). Use the `servers` variables below to point this
  document at a real host.

### Authentication

Authentication is **off by default**. When `server.bearer_token` is set,
`GET /metrics` requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and returns `401`
otherwise. `/` and `/healthz` stay open on purpose, so a load balancer or
uptime check does not need the shared secret.

Because the endpoint discloses hostnames, mount points and network
interfaces, treat it as internal: firewall the port to the Prometheus
server first, and use the token and TLS as defence in depth.

### Request methods

Routes are registered without method filters, so `HEAD` works and other
methods are not rejected. Prometheus only ever issues `GET`, which is what
this document describes.

scheme.description: https when the agent is configured with a TLS certificate and key.

host.description: Hostname or IP address of the monitored server.

port.description: Value of server.listen_address in the agent config.

get.description:
Returns the current value of every enabled collector in the Prometheus
text exposition format.

Metrics are gathered **lazily, once per request** — the agent reads no
counters between scrapes. Each collector runs concurrently and is
bounded by `server.scrape_timeout` (default 15s); set the Prometheus
job's `scrape_timeout` higher than that value.

A collector that fails does not fail the response. Its series are
omitted and `watchcat_scrape_success{collector="..."}` reports `0`,
which is the series to alert on.

Content negotiation follows the `Accept` header. Sending
`application/openmetrics-text; version=1.0.0` returns OpenMetrics
(terminated by an `# EOF` line); anything else returns the classic
text format. The exact response types are:

- `text/plain; version=0.0.4; charset=utf-8; escaping=underscores`
- `application/openmetrics-text; version=1.0.0; charset=utf-8; escaping=underscores`

`Accept-Encoding: gzip` is honoured and answered with
`Content-Encoding: gzip`.

At most 4 scrapes are served concurrently; further requests get `503`
rather than queueing.

200.description: Metrics in the Prometheus exposition format.

text/plain.example:
# HELP watchcat_agent_build_info Build metadata of the running agent. Always 1.
# TYPE watchcat_agent_build_info gauge
watchcat_agent_build_info{build_date="2026-08-26T03:55:16Z",commit="none",goversion="go1.26.3",version="v0.1.0"} 1
# HELP watchcat_cpu_seconds_total Seconds the CPUs spent in each mode.
# TYPE watchcat_cpu_seconds_total counter
watchcat_cpu_seconds_total{cpu="all",mode="idle"} 1.0490672e+06
watchcat_cpu_seconds_total{cpu="all",mode="system"} 92944.05
watchcat_cpu_seconds_total{cpu="all",mode="user"} 142238.16
# HELP watchcat_memory_total_bytes Total installed physical memory.
# TYPE watchcat_memory_total_bytes gauge
watchcat_memory_total_bytes 6.8719476736e+10
# HELP watchcat_memory_available_bytes Memory available for new applications without swapping.
# TYPE watchcat_memory_available_bytes gauge
watchcat_memory_available_bytes 1.9743305728e+10
# HELP watchcat_filesystem_size_bytes Total size of the filesystem.
# TYPE watchcat_filesystem_size_bytes gauge
watchcat_filesystem_size_bytes{device="/dev/disk3s1s1",fstype="apfs",mountpoint="/"} 9.94662584320e+11
# HELP watchcat_scrape_success 1 if the source was collected without error, 0 otherwise.
# TYPE watchcat_scrape_success gauge
watchcat_scrape_success{collector="cpu"} 1
watchcat_scrape_success{collector="filesystem"} 1

application/openmetrics-text.example:
# TYPE watchcat_memory_total_bytes gauge
# HELP watchcat_memory_total_bytes Total installed physical memory.
watchcat_memory_total_bytes 6.8719476736e+10
# EOF

500.description:
No metrics could be gathered at all. Partial failures return `200`
with `watchcat_scrape_success` at `0` instead.

text/plain.example: An error has occurred while serving metrics:

503.description:
Either the collection exceeded `server.scrape_timeout`, or more than
4 scrapes were already in flight. Both are retryable.

overloaded.value: Limit of concurrent requests reached (4), try again later.

get.description:
Returns `200 ok` whenever the HTTP listener is up. Deliberately
unauthenticated so load balancers, Kubernetes probes and uptime checks
work without the shared secret.

This is a **liveness** check, not a readiness check: it reports that the
agent is serving, and does not run the collectors. To alert on whether
metrics are actually usable, use `watchcat_scrape_success` from
`/metrics` or Prometheus' own `up` series.

A small HTML page naming the build, the metrics path and the enabled
collectors — what you get from opening the port in a browser. Not
intended for machine consumption; parse `/metrics` instead.

Only the exact path `/` is served. Any other unregistered path returns
`404`.

text/html.example:
watchcat-agent

watchcat-agent v0.1.0 (commit none, built 2026-08-26T03:55:16Z, go1.26.3, linux/amd64)

Metrics: /metrics

Health: /healthz

Enabled collectors: cpu, memory, filesystem, diskio, network, load, host, process

bearerAuth.description:
Shared secret from `server.bearer_token` (or the `WATCHCAT_BEARER_TOKEN`
environment variable). Compared in constant time, so a wrong token
leaks nothing through response timing.

In Prometheus, supply it with:

```yaml
authorization:
  type: Bearer
  credentials_file: /etc/prometheus/watchcat.token
```

The credentials file must not contain a trailing newline.

Accept.name: Accept
Accept.description: Selects the exposition format. Prometheus sends this automatically.

AcceptEncoding.name: Accept-Encoding
AcceptEncoding.description: Send `gzip` to have the response compressed.

ContentEncoding.description: Present as `gzip` when the client offered gzip in `Accept-Encoding`.

Unauthorized.description:
`server.bearer_token` is configured and the request carried no
`Authorization` header, or one that did not match exactly.

NotFound.description: No route is registered at this path.

PrometheusExposition.title: Prometheus exposition format
PrometheusExposition.description:
Line-oriented plain text, not JSON. Each metric is preceded by `# HELP`
and `# TYPE` comments, then one line per series:
`name{label="value",...} <float> [timestamp]`.

Every series this agent emits is prefixed `watchcat_`, except the Go
runtime metrics (`go_*`) contributed when `collectors.go` is enabled.
Counters are cumulative — apply `rate()` in PromQL rather than reading
them directly.

Specification: https://prometheus.io/docs/instrumenting/exposition_formats/
PrometheusExposition.example:
# HELP watchcat_load1 1 minute load average.
# TYPE watchcat_load1 gauge
watchcat_load1 2.4423828125
